items.stem: Which cmdlet changes a property, such as the send-size limit, on an existing Exchange Online mailbox?

options.rationale: Correct: Set-Mailbox changes properties on an existing mailbox.
Get-Mailbox reads properties but does not change them.
New-Mailbox creates a mailbox rather than changing an existing one.

items.explanation: Correct: Set-Mailbox changes properties on an existing mailbox.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about managing Exchange Online are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: You connect to Exchange Online PowerShell using the ExchangeOnlineManagement module
Get-Mailbox can return many properties with Format-List
options.rationale: Correct: piping to Format-List shows the mailbox's properties.

options.text: PowerShell cannot be used for Exchange Online administration
options.rationale: Incorrect: PowerShell is a primary administration interface for Exchange Online.

options.text: Set-Mailbox is used only to read mailbox size
options.rationale: Incorrect: Set-Mailbox changes properties; reading is done with Get-Mailbox.

items.explanation: Correct: the ExchangeOnlineManagement module connects PowerShell, and Get-Mailbox with Format-List lists properties.

items.stem: To give an administrator the ability to open and read all user mailboxes, which permission is granted?

options.rationale: Correct: Full Access lets the grantee open the mailbox and its contents.
Send As lets a user send as the mailbox but not read its contents.
Mail flow rules govern message routing, not mailbox access.
Group membership does not grant mailbox access rights.

items.explanation: Correct: Full Access, granted with Add-MailboxPermission, lets the grantee open the mailbox.
